mainEntity.name: Can a Robotic Case Packer Handle Pouches, Trays and Thermoformed Packages in the Same Line?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, within its validated range. TRFRapidpack handles pouches, pillow bags, flow packs, thermoformed packages, trays, cartons, cups, tubs and small packaged products, and changes products and patterns through recipes with reduced mechanical adjustments. Packages with very different shapes may need another end-of-arm tool, so TRF validates the full package list before quoting.

mainEntity.name: Does a Case Packer Need Vision-Guided Robotics for High-Mix Production?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always. Vision-guided handling helps when products arrive in variable positions or need orientation, which is common on high-mix cosmetics lines. TRFRapidpack offers vision-guided or indexed handling. When products arrive in a fixed position and patterns repeat, indexed handling, TRFOnepack or the gravity loading of TRFDroppack can be simpler options.

mainEntity.name: Can a Cobot Palletizer Handle Multiple SKUs and Pallet Patterns?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. For cosmetics palletizing, TRFCobot stores multiple recipes, pallet patterns and SKU changes for lines of about 1 to 10 cases per minute with cases up to about 22 lb. Each recipe holds the case data and pallet pattern for one product, so a shade or size change is a selection on the screen. Higher rates move to TRFCompact or TRFSpeed.

mainEntity.name: Can a Conveyor System Integrate With My Palletizer and Case Packer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A case conveyor system such as TRFIntraflow includes sensors, PLC and HMI, barcode and vision interfaces, machine communication and palletizer interfaces, so the conveying, the case packer and the palletizer run as one flow. TRF engineers the conveyors around your production flow and layout, never as loose components, and defines each interface during project engineering.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between a Merge, a Divert and a Sorting Conveyor?

acceptedAnswer.text: A merge combines cases from several lines into one lane, a divert moves cases from one lane to another, and a sorting conveyor sends each case to its destination based on identification such as a barcode. In personal care plants, these modules let retail, club and e-commerce cases follow their own lanes to the palletizer.

mainEntity.name: How Is ROI Estimated for Switching From Manual to Robotic Case Packing?

acceptedAnswer.text: ROI depends on the labor hours case packing takes today across shifts, local labor cost and the installed cost of the system, plus the capacity the line gains when packing stops limiting it. Seasonal and promotional peaks should be counted in annual hours, not peak-week hours. A TRF Sales Engineer builds the estimate with your line data.
